purpose: Gilteritinib is used to treat a type of blood cancer called acute myeloid leukemia (AML) in adults whose cancer has a specific gene change called a FLT3 mutation. It is used when the leukemia has come back after treatment or has stopped responding to other treatments. Your doctor will test your cancer to make sure this drug is right for you.
how_it_works: Your leukemia cells have an abnormal protein called FLT3 that tells the cancer to grow out of control. Gilteritinib works like a targeted 'off switch' that blocks this faulty protein. By blocking FLT3, the medication slows down or stops the cancer cells from growing and dividing.
common_side_effects: Feeling very tired or weak, muscle or joint pain, nausea, constipation, diarrhea, swelling in your hands or feet, dizziness, low blood pressure, shortness of breath, and elevated liver levels on blood tests.
warnings: This medicine can cause a serious condition called differentiation syndrome, which can be life-threatening — watch for fever, difficulty breathing, or sudden weight gain and call your doctor right away. It can also cause a dangerous heart rhythm problem called QT prolongation, so your doctor will monitor your heart. Do not use if you are pregnant or breastfeeding, as it can harm an unborn baby. Tell your doctor about all other medications you take, as many drugs can interact with gilteritinib.
typical_dosing: The usual dose is one 120 mg tablet taken by mouth once a day, with or without food. Try to take it at the same time each day. Keep taking it as directed even if you feel well, and never stop without talking to your doctor first.
